We have several members who are pupils at this school and the winner of the race was none other than Doug Maclean of our own Club, who this time was running for his school. G.

This race was held over our own course this year and our lads duly celebrated this fact by winning the individual and team honours in great style. Doug Maclean in his last race as a youth, came home an easy winner by about 150 yards, and our young road race winner, G.

The first race for the “Overseas” Cup took place at Wimbledon on January 13th, and was run over our usual 3½ miles course. Quite a good field turned out to race for this very fine new addition to our list of club trophies and the winner proved to be G.
Our Youths journeyed to Purley on January 27th for a match against the John Fisher School. It was decided to score six a side and although we had the first lad home in G.
In a six a side triangular match we came out on top with a score of 31 points, with Southgate H. 63, and the Boys' Training Company 96. G.

Wright beat Hewson of Mitcham in the half-mile, and this youngster is a champion of the future, while Geoff Goode met his match in Boyd of the home club in the 1 mile.

Godfrey won the 880 yards and Frank Kemp obliged, as usual, in the 220, with Geoff Goode taking the mile. We also won the sprint relay, and final points for the junior match were:—Belgrave, 19; Mitcham, 13; S.L.H., 4.
Geoff Goode won the 1 mile, with Brian Trower second, and the latter looks like following in his brother's footsteps as a future club champion.

Geoff Goode and Brian Trower were first two home in the mile and Trower also won the Javelin event, much to his surprise ! Jim Purdy won the High Jump and also gained third place in the Javelin, while Frank Kemp won the Shott Putt and it was a case of everyone having a go at everything !
Don Maclean won the junior mile, as expected, and from the way he went off he seemed quite determined to make sure that Geoff Goode had no reserves of speed left.

Geoff Goode was first home followed by Peter Courtney, who was running for the school, then came Frank Wright followed by four more Belgravians.
Geoff Goode improved on last year's third position by finishing as runner-up to I. Boyd of Wallington County School, with Frank Wright in third place.
At Wimbledon on January 12th Geoff Goode retained his hold on the " Overseas " Cup by a comfortable margin.

This was against the Oxford and Bermondsey Club on January 19th and owing to the fact that our visitors were late in arriving, it was actually a Youths' team that we fielded. Geoff Goode, Frank Wright and G. Lines came home together in first place followed by V.
Held at Wimbledon on January 26th this was a 7 aside match with the Sutton & Cheam lads. Geoff Goode was first home followed by Frank Wright with R.

Geoff Goode ran the first stage of about 3 miles in 18.15 and gave us a good lead from Highgate, Wycombe & Finchley H. Gerry Lines was our next runner and he kept the lead and did 18.54, with Ron Linstead going next and he clocked 19 mins. dead and we were still ahead of Wycombe, Highgate and Finchley.
The Sutton lads reversed the previous result and this time came out on top with 35 pts. to our 47. Geoff Goode was content to run in behind a local lad and he was followed by Gerry Lines, with J.

Frank Wright managed to get up with the leaders once again but Geoff Goode found the effort too much for him and was our 4th scoring man. This race is certainly a " hoodoo " for Geoff and Micky Pyer must have been disappointed at our 4th place in the team race, but we hope for better luck next year.

Geoff Goode was 4th in the 1 mile team race and our team occupied the same position, but D. Maddicks won the junior Javelin with a throw of 144ft. 7in.

The 1 mile junior saw the biggest field of the whole meeting, and with such promising youngsters to call upon the Club should have no fear as regards the future. Geoff. Goode ran in his usual plucky style to win in 4 min. 31.6 secs., with G.

Ron Linstead had received an injury during a training run, G.Goode had a severe cold and Frank Wright was unable to get leave. However the rest of the lads had a good try but could do no better than 20th out of the 24 teams.

In the 1 mile Virr of T.V.H. struck out early and was followed by Geoff Goode for a couple of laps. On the last lap Jon Burr passed the latter and if he had had a baton might have also caught his rival of the Brighton road.
